evidence.mission_note: A manual 6-cylinder Z3 roadster priced at the bottom of the ideal band is squarely the primary enthusiast-bridge target. Its fit depends on the VIN confirming a true 3.0i and on documented cooling and rear-structure health.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes a factory-manual, 6-cylinder facelift Z3 roadster in a metallic blue consistent with Topaz, asking $10,000, below the $10,968-$13,976 fair-value band. Photos support good cosmetic condition: glossy paint, an uncracked tan dash, a tidy cabin and a clean stock engine bay. The M steering wheel and a Michelin Pilot Sport All Season tire are visible. Against that, the title labels it a 2000 3.0i, a year/engine pairing that does not exist in the US market without a production-date explanation, and no VIN is given to resolve it. Clean title, two owners, no accidents and the itemised recent service are all seller text with no receipts or history report. Neither model-critical item is addressed: there is no cooling-system history (the reservoir appears aged in photos) and no evidence on the rear subframe or trunk floor. The car has sat for many months, including a brief pending status in October, which is worth asking about.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the VIN and photos of the trunk floor and underside, then run the VIN decode and a history report before discussing a Sarasota-area PPI.
